correctness.rationale: The adjacency algebra of a diameter-d distance-regular graph has d+1 spectral idempotents E_j, constant diagonal m_j/v and offdiagonal (m_j/v)c_j(distance). For j>0, if |c_j(r)|=1, Cauchy–Schwarz makes columns E_j e_z collinear along each edge in connected distance graph G_r; therefore rank E_j=1. A nonprincipal rank-one idempotent with equal diagonal entries would force constant or alternating ± signs along adjacent vertices, implying principal eigenspace or bipartiteness. The latter contradicts G_2 connected (d≥2), while d=1 yields K_v with v≥3. Hence |c_j(r)|<1 and two independent absorber columns in each nonprincipal eigenspace, plus one principal dimension, produce dimB=2d+1. The orthogonal complement is invariant and dark; strictly positive decay rates eliminate nondecaying eigenvectors on B, even with Jordan blocks, yielding capture η_x=⟨x|P_B|x⟩. Inverting the 2×2 spectral Gram matrices proves the site formula and mixed mean (2d+1)/v. Independent spectral/Krylov tests over all 45 Petersen absorber pairs found dimension 5 and max site-projection discrepancy 1.67e−15; this is supplementary to the general spectral proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General Krylov reduction is an algorithm for an arbitrary adjacency and marked set, but does not yield rank 2d+1 for every primitive distance-regular graph nor the three-distance closed site formula without the nonstandard connected-distance-graph argument. Multimarked spatial search uses a Hermitian oracle rather than irreversible capture.

value.rationale: The bright subspace rank and exact site-resolved absorption law are natural observables for irreversible quantum transport on symmetric networks. The strict primitive-cosine separation lemma yields a uniform exact formula over all diameters and absorber separations without relying on vertex-transitivity. It sharpens general Krylov prescriptions by replacing site-specific computation with graph spectral cosine data.

final_claim: On every finite primitive distance-regular graph with all distance graphs connected, two positive-rate absorbing vertices generate exactly a 2d+1-dimensional bright space, with a placement-independent mixed-state capture probability and explicit three-distance sitewise cosine-sequence formula.
limitations: A stronger published Bose–Mesner controllability theorem may subsume the rank assertion under alternate vocabulary.
Hypothesis that every distance graph is connected is essential; imprimitive, more than two sinks, zero loss rates and finite-time capture are excluded.
